output.summary: KEP-5882 proposes a new `.spec.podReplacementPolicy` field on Deployments so users can choose whether new pods are created only after terminating pods finish or immediately. The KEP is in implementable status at alpha stage.
output.rationale: Deployments handle terminating pods inconsistently: Recreate waits for terminating pods, while RollingUpdate and scale-up do not, so pod count can exceed spec.replicas. This causes extra node autoscaling, slower rollouts under contention, and lost visibility into work done by terminating pods. The KEP adds a per-Deployment policy, modeled on the Job field, to let users pick the behavior.

alternatives.option: Implement the behavior in a separate controller that manages ReplicaSets
alternatives.why_not: The KEP says there is a need for this to be implemented by the Deployment controller, because many existing workloads can benefit from this feature.

alternatives.option: Model the field on Job's podReplacementPolicy (KEP-3939)
alternatives.why_not: Not rejected: the KEP explicitly builds the field as similar to Job's podReplacementPolicy.

evidence.quote: This KEP proposes to add a new field `.spec.podReplacementPolicy` to Deployments to allow users to specify the desired behavior.
The Recreate Deployment strategy waits for terminating pods to terminate before creating (scheduling) new pods.
The RollingUpdate deployment strategy does not wait for terminating pods and creates (schedules) new pods immediately.
This KEP proposes to introduce a new `.spec.podReplacementPolicy` field (similar to Job's `.spec.podReplacementPolicy` in [kubernetes/enhancements#3939]
There is a need for this feature to be implemented by a Deployment controller, because many existing workloads can benefit from this feature.
